chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and Salama the seller of the Sabiri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when he took the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) and looked into it, would say: 'Who can endure this? Who can endure this?' Then he would act upon it. And when he would stand for the prayer, his complexion would change to the extent that it became recognizable on his face. And no one from his sons after him could endure the actions of Ali (peace be upon him) except Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

key_terms.تَغَيَّرَ لَوْنُهُ: His complexion changed (indicating intense emotion or spiritual state)
key_terms.كِتَابُ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali (referring to the Quran or a specific compilation of his teachings)

ai.seo_question: What was the physical reaction of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi underscores the unique spiritual capacity of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) to internalize and implement the rigorous teachings of his father, Imam Ali (AS), a feat unmatched by other descendants. The physical transformation of his complexion during prayer illustrates the intense awe (khushu') and contemplation of divine majesty that characterized his worship, linking the burden of knowledge to the depth of practice. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that true adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt requires not just intellectual acceptance but a transformative spiritual state mirroring the Imams' own devotion.
